chunks: Ali, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from al-Harith ibn al-Mughira, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Perform Qunut in every two Rak'at, obligatory or optional, before the Ruku'.'
ai.seo_question: When and how should Qunut be performed in daily prayers according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility and recommended timing of Qunut in the two-rak'at prayers, specifying it should be recited before Ruku'. In Shia jurisprudence, this supports the view that Qunut is a Sunnah mu'akkadah (emphasized tradition) rather than a mandatory pillar, allowing for flexibility in its recitation during both Fajr and other two-rak'at prayers.

en.hubeali: Ali, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Al Haris Bin Al Mugheira who said,
‘Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Perform Qunut in every two Rak’at (of Salāt), Obligatory or optional, before the Rukū’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from Muhammad ibn Fudayl from al-Harith ibn al- Mughirah who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Say Qunut (supplication after recitation in second Rak‘at) before Ruku‘ (bowing down on one’s knees) in every two Rak‘at in obligatory Salah (prayer) or optional ones’”
